title: Mount St. Helens, 1980: the man who had seconds to warn the world

lines: This man has seconds to warn the world.
Nineteen eighty. Volcanologist David Johnston is watching Mount Saint Helens from six miles away.
Magma has swollen its north face outward, five feet a day.
At eight thirty-two, an earthquake shakes it loose: the biggest landslide ever recorded.
That uncorks it like a shaken soda. It explodes sideways, at three hundred miles an hour.
Harry Truman, eighty-three, had refused to leave his lodge.
Fifty-seven people died. But scientists like David had fought to close the mountain. That likely saved thousands.
